output.summary: Approved G1022 design revision 2: the default graph goes from 26 to 15 nodes. review_design applies the seven design lenses in one reviewer with adversary_design beside it; review_impl applies compliance, correctness, missing (searching the goal's own commit), tests and craft; both feed G1000's filters. Lenses are declared per node (`lenses`), removed per goal with skip keys `<node>:<lens>`; intent, simplicity, compliance, missing and craft are mandatory. Budget default follows the existing formula (60 -> 27, same rounds per subject). Depends on 1000, 1020, 1017 and edits docs/design in its own PR; rollout via the lens policy branch and G1024's notice; engine version is the next minor at merge. review_design approved after one round of four findings; no owner questions under the owner's undo-reach test.

Revision 2 of the consolidated-review design (15 nodes: review_design with seven lenses plus a separate adversary_design into filter_design; review_impl with compliance, correctness, missing, tests and craft into filter_impl; project lenses via a `lenses` node field, goal removal via `<node>:<lens>` skip keys, a `lens` finding tag). It answers review_design attempt 1. F1: Missing and code review search `code.commit`, not read_dev. F2: G1017 case 3 is adopted, so this PR edits docs/design with a HISTORY row and deletes its pending row. F3: rollout to other repositories goes through G1024's policy_update item, and the version is the next minor at merge. F4: review_impl drops `spec`, so migration is budget-free, and the stale keys and test 11 are corrected. It also adds a G1025 interaction section, restores the security/code_quality instructions on review_impl and renames Graph.lenses to Graph.reviewers.

Resubmit after base rebased G1022 onto dev 5288bf7 (G1028 merged). Conflicts resolved keeping both goals: ENGINE_VERSION 1.3.0 (G1028 keeps FOLLOWS_SINCE 1.2.0); card.py keeps G1028's carried findings, closed-id split, follows and --repo with G1022's lenses checklist and lens hint; schemas.py FINDING_KEYS has both follows and lens; add-goal SKILL keeps G1029's intent check and G1022's lens skip text; CLI_USAGE, lens_intent.md and HISTORY merged; MIGRATING's G1022 section says 1.3. One frozen test adjusted in the tests commit as a semantic-conflict resolution (approved by review_tests). test_engine_review_lenses 59/59, findings_rounds 30/30, card_budget, design_docs, agent_plugin, prompt_stats pass.

findings.text: F1 (material): the Missing lens searches the wrong tree. The experiment reviewers had a full worktree at the submission, which is how GT1 was found. The shipped review_impl has only the code checkpoint view and read_dev, the integration tip, and the review instruction says to check claims against read_dev. For a stacked goal (G1022 itself), read_dev lacks the dependency code. Fix: lens_missing.md (and the review instruction, for code) searches the subject commit with git grep <pattern> <code.commit> and git show <code.commit>:<path>; or the checkpoint view gains a grep command. Add a card-snapshot test and a caveat in A.5.

F2 (material): not aligned with G1017's current design. G1017 makes G1022 depend on [1000, 1020, 1017] and requires G1022's PR to edit docs/design, add a HISTORY section 4 row and delete its pending row. This design puts SPEC/DESIGN text out of scope (section 11), assumes G1022 may merge first (section 12) and orders delivery without G1017 (section 8). G1017's row also understates the sections: it is missing SPEC 3.3, 3.6, 4.8, 4.10, 4.18, 4.20, 5.4 and 8.3. Fix: adopt case 3 now (depends_on, in-scope docs/design edits listed from section 12, a guard test, G1017 in the delivery order and the release window), and add a follow-up that sends G1017 the full section list.

F3 (material): the rollout ignores G1024, the only way other bootstrapped repositories learn that the default graph changed. Fix: section 8 names G1024's policy_update item as the notice and MIGRATING 'Adopting the consolidated graph' as its procedure. Decide that the release shipping the 15-node template includes G1024. Hand G1024 three points: added and removed template files (review.md, the lens prompts, removed review_design.md/review_impl.md); workflow.json restructuring needs MIGRATING, not a text merge; this repository's record is created or refreshed by zzzops/policy/lenses if G1024 lands first. Phrase ENGINE_VERSION and the floor as 'the next minor at merge', since G1024 may also need a bump.

F4: the migration claim and test 11 are wrong. A carried-over review_design has stale_keys [def, lenses, policy.intent], not [def] (still uncounted). review_impl gains a spec input, so inputs.spec is stale and frontier.counts charges the re-run to the budget, contrary to section 8. Fix: correct section 8 and test 11, and either accept and document one counted run per in-flight goal past implement, or drop spec from review_impl. For the 26-node path, MIGRATING should say to set an explicit budget first, since the default limit falls from 60 to 27.

output.summary: Revision 2 resolves all four prior findings. The Missing lens searches code.commit; G1017 case 3 is adopted with in-PR docs/design edits; the G1024 notice path and version rule are added; the migration stale keys are corrected and review_impl's spec input is dropped. §8a matches G1025's spec. No new findings and no owner questions: the remaining choices are bounded or have a clear winner.

Approved: the 15-node graph, the lenses field, <node>:<lens> skips, lens tags, the lenses fingerprint and budget exemption, the card checklist, approval and PR display and docs match design rev 2. Both reported departures are sound: the redefined-input exemption is exactly the inputs the definition added or removed (confirmed with a probe), and lenses.text uses the same INLINE/blob rule as prompt. Tests are not weakened. Notes: a stale paired-skip example in DESIGN §4.1, the config number in SPEC §4.10, and that rebasing to 1.3.0 must also update the HISTORY row and three MIGRATING mentions.

Approved after the rebase onto dev with G1028. The range-diff shows exactly one test changed (test_skipping_the_lens_of_an_open_finding_keeps_it), updated to G1028's stale-review carry; all other assertions kept and no-finding-lost purpose intact; no fixture or import changes.

spec:
Follow-up to G1000, from the owner's direction after a second lens experiment (2026-11-01). G1000 ships seven lens nodes per subject (26 nodes). The experiment showed a single reviewer working through several lenses matches or beats separate lens agents at about a quarter of the cost, because every separate agent repeats the discovery work.

Evidence (scratchpad implx/RESULTS.md and run/exp/replay_multi_scores.md; restate the numbers in the design appendix, since the scratchpad is not in the repo):
- Implementation, G1016 attempt 1 with 6 planted defects plus its real review_impl defect (a duplicated capability rule in render.py, outside the diff). Five separate implementation lenses: 6/7 for 337k tokens. The seven copied design lenses: 6/7 for 436k. The old single reviewer: 5/7 for 86k. No separate lens found the real defect. One multi-lens reviewer (Compliance, Correctness, Missing, Tests, Craft), three runs: 7, 7 and 6 of 7, at 82-87k each, finding the real defect in 2 of 3 runs. The Missing lens alone found it as material.
- Design, revision 6 stacked-delivery replay (12 known defects). Seven separate lenses: 7/12 for ~245k. One multi-lens reviewer: 4/12 per run (41k each). One multi-lens run plus a separate Adversary: 7/12 for ~76k.

Change the shipped default graph:
1. Design review: one multi-lens reviewer node with the seven design lenses (intent, simplicity, truth, adversary, concurrency, rollout, experience) and one separate `adversary_design` node, both feeding `filter_design`.
2. Implementation review: one multi-lens reviewer node with the implementation lenses Compliance (including changed interfaces), Correctness (including security), Missing (outside the diff: other implementations, callers, docs, prompts and config sharing the changed rule), Tests and Craft, feeding `filter_impl`. Findings carry a `lens` tag.
3. Keep G1000's engine work: the filter (promote, never demote), impact/material, skip refusal, project intent and previous.changed. The reviewer prompts must tell the reviewer to work lens by lens and not stop at the first problems.
4. Lens selection stays user-configurable: a goal (and a project's workflow.json) chooses which lenses the multi-lens reviewer applies, and Intent, Simplicity/Craft and Missing cannot be removed. Decide in the design whether this is a node input, a goal field or the skip mechanism, and show it on approval items and in the PR body.
5. Migration: G1000's lens policy branch for this repository must adopt this graph instead of the 26-node graph if it has not landed yet. Otherwise this goal's rollout says how in-flight goals move from lens nodes to the consolidated nodes.

Acceptance:
- The template graph validates; the node count and review fan-in are tested.
- Card snapshots show the lens checklist on both reviewer cards, and the `lens` tag in output_schema.
- A test shows a goal removing an optional lens, and a refusal when it tries to remove a mandatory one.
- prompt_stats budgets hold.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes (§7 graph and the sections G1017's pending row lists), adds a HISTORY §4 row and deletes the G1022 pending row (G1017's rule).
- G1003's dogfood run re-scores the consolidated set on real goals.
title: Consolidate review lenses: one multi-lens reviewer per subject, plus a separate design Adversary
